facts.fact_text: In the evening of 24 February 2014, a public gathering in support of the convicted activists took place at Tverskaya Street in Moscow.
In the evening of 24 February 2014, a public gathering in support of the convicted activists took place at Malaya Sadovaya Street in St Petersburg.
The applicants took part in the public meetings on 24 February 2014 at Tverskaya Street in Moscow and at Malaya Sadovaya Street in St Petersburg.
There is no information that the public meetings on 24 February 2014 at Tverskaya Street in Moscow and at Malaya Sadovaya Street in St Petersburg turned violent.
The protesters at the public meetings on 24 February 2014 shouted political slogans.
The police warned the protesters at the public meetings on 24 February 2014 through megaphones that the gatherings had not been authorised.
The police instructed the protesters at the public meetings on 24 February 2014 to disperse.
The applicants were apprehended and transferred to various police stations following the public meetings on 24 February 2014.

On the dates stipulated in the appended table, the applicants were convicted under Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences for breaching the procedure for the organisation or conduct of public gatherings.
The applicants were sentenced to fines ranging between 10,000 Russian roubles (RUB 10,000) and RUB 20,000, as set out in the appended table.
The applicant in application no. 3093/15 was convicted under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences for a refusal to obey a lawful order of a police officer.
The applicant in application no. 3093/15 was ordered to pay RUB 1,000.
For a summary of the relevant domestic law, see Navalnyy v. Russia [GC] (nos. 29580/12 and 4 others, §§ 46-47, 15 November 2018).
The domestic legal provisions governing administrative transfer (escorting) and detention are set out in the case of Butkevich v. Russia (no. 5865/07, §§ 33-36, 13 February 2018).
The authorities had not been notified of the public gatherings on 24 February 2014 at Tverskaya Street in Moscow and at Malaya Sadovaya Street in St Petersburg.
